$comment: Mission 1.74.5. The second approval for the second question, after the first one was exhausted by an attempt that bounced. It sits BESIDE the packet, names it by a recomputed hash, and authorises exactly one manual send.

approval.why: Mission 1.66. An approval flag written into the frozen packet would change the artifact the operator read, and the packet's own gate asserts that the packet records no approval. That field means THIS DOCUMENT RECORDS NO APPROVAL and never that no approval exists.
approval.why_it_was_recomputed_rather_than_copied: the operator's message carries a digest, and copying it would make the approval name whatever the instruction said rather than whatever the packet is. Recomputing turns a quoted string into a check: if the two had disagreed the approval would have been refused rather than recorded.

approved_action.$comment: Mission 1.65's envelope rule. The digest binds the ACTION and excludes itself, the execution status, the recorded date and the sender.
approved_action.approved_subject: Terms scope: HEAD measurements of publicly reachable third-party websites
approved_action.why_the_sender_is_not_pinned: the operator stated the sending mailbox is chosen at execution time, which is the same property Mission 1.65 recorded in advance for a manual mail send: the sender is not determined until the send. The cost is unchanged -- this approval pins the action apart from the mailbox it leaves from.

execution.$comment: An approval says an action MAY be performed. Nothing has been performed.
execution.why_byte_verification_is_unreachable_her: still a manual mail send, so still Mission 1.66's ceiling: the send happens in a mail client nothing in this repository can observe. The channel changed from the designated address to the published one and the OBSERVABILITY did not, because the ceiling is a property of the medium rather than of the address.
execution.upgrade_path: NONE for this channel. A future mission may record OPERATOR_ATTESTED and nothing above it.
execution.reachable_only_through: an explicit operator attestation that the message was sent, plus the sending mailbox, which no frozen document contains.

relationship_to_the_exhausted_approval.$comment: The first approval is not reused, not reinterpreted, and not repaired. It records what happened to it.
relationship_to_the_exhausted_approval.why: the recipient differs, and the recipient is a bound field, so this authorises a different action rather than extending a spent one. The two approvals name different content digests and neither can stand in for the other.

recommended_next_action.action: the operator sends one email to d@globalping.io with the approved subject and the frozen body, from a mailbox of their choosing, then attests to it
